subject: Recap & pricing follow-up: serving-mode trade-offs (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)

Subject: Recap & pricing follow-up: serving-mode trade-offs (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)

Alex / Atlas procurement team — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap of what I heard and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth. Please reply with any corrections.

Summary of AtlasAI requirements from call:
- Target feature: contextual search + short-form generation in customer support UI (expected 90th-pct latency target < 300ms).
- Throughput profile: average 20 qps with peak bursts to ~100 qps during business hours.
- Token volume estimate: 10M – 200M tokens/month (uncertain; tracking growth).
- Data controls: PII-sensitive logs; must meet contractual data isolation and optional customer-managed keys (KMS).
- Budget note: finance asked for a defensible comparison of per-token vs reserved capacity economics to present next week.

Immediate asks / next steps I promised:
1) I attached a cost model (ATLAS_cost_model_v2.xlsx) with a comparative view — can you confirm the 3 volume scenarios (10M / 50M / 200M) are reasonable?
2) We will provide three concrete configs with pricing: Hosted API (pay-as-you-go), Dedicated (reserved commits + burst), and Private (VPC or on-prem) including one-time onboarding and KMS/HSM line items.
3) If Atlas prefers, we'll propose a short Dedicated pilot (2 months) to validate latency/cost before committing to long-term reserved capacity.

Questions for you (helps tighten model):
- Do you have a preferred procurement cadence (PO in 2 weeks / 30–60 day review)?
- Any minimum SLA or compliance addenda (SOC2 + custom DPA) required now?

I’m looping in Rishi and Connor (solutions) to craft the pricing scenarios and a recommended baseline. Expect a detailed reply with numbers later today or tomorrow.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

- Atlas is leaning toward Dedicated capacity because predictable latency is important for the product UX, but we also need a VPC/private endpoint for legal/regulatory reasons. If Dedicated can provide tenant isolation + VPC, that would be our preference.
- Procurement asked for a side-by-side showing: (a) per-token hosted cost, (b) committed Dedicated monthly cost (with reserved commit sizes), and (c) a rough on-prem baseline (CAPEX + OPEX) to justify Private.
- Timeline: procurement wants preliminary numbers by 12/10 to include in an internal review with the CFO.

Can you include examples for 10M, 50M, and 200M tokens/month? Also call out any additional per-account fees (network egress, KMS, audit logs retention).

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-06T16:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Recap & pricing follow-up — tiered cost scenarios (attached)

Team — I updated the spreadsheet (ATLAS_cost_model_v2.xlsx) and summarized the results below for quick consumption. I included conservative assumptions and a sensitivity column for longer context. Notes on assumptions: 1 token ~ 4 bytes avg; model mix assumed 70% embed/retrieval + 30% generation; Dedicated GPU sizing based on our p4d/p3-equivalent offering for this workload.

Summary (effective $/1k tokens, after amortizing fixed fees):
- Scenario A — 10M tokens/mo:
  * Hosted (pay-as-you-go): approx $16 / 1k tokens -> total ~$160.00 (note: small volumes penalized by per-request overhead).
  * Dedicated (small reserved): reserved commit = 0.5 GPU equivalent (~5k qps tokens capacity): monthly reserved fee $6,500 + per-token infra $0.004 -> effective ~$6.50 / 1k tokens -> total ~$65.
  * Private (on-prem amortized over 36 months): initial HW + setup ~$160,000 capex -> amortized ~$4,444/mo + ops ~$2,000/mo -> effective ~$250+ / 1k tokens (very high at low volume).

- Scenario B — 50M tokens/mo:
  * Hosted: approx $4.5 / 1k tokens -> total ~$225.
  * Dedicated (medium reserved): reserved commit = 2 GPUs equivalent: monthly reserved fee $24,000 + infra delta -> effective ~$1.10 / 1k tokens -> total ~$55.
  * Private (amortized): effective ~$55 / 1k tokens (approaching parity if Atlas runs at sustained 50M+ and takes on ops).

- Scenario C — 200M tokens/mo:
  * Hosted: approx $2.2 / 1k tokens -> total ~$440.
  * Dedicated (large reserved): reserved commit = 8 GPUs equivalent: monthly reserved fee $85,000 + infra delta -> effective ~$0.36 / 1k tokens -> total ~$72.
  * Private (amortized): effective ~$18–$30 / 1k tokens depending on utilization and ops model (could be lower than Dedicated at extremely large sustained volumes but requires heavy operational investment).

Other items to call out:
- Burst & availability: Dedicated includes burst pool for spikes (charged only on use) and an SLA for 99.9% availability; Hosted offers simpler onboarding and no provisioning lead time but less isolation.
- Data controls: Hosted (logical isolation + optional CMK) covers many compliance use-cases quickly. Dedicated + VPC gives stronger tenancy isolation and private endpoints; Private on-prem gives the most control (and the longest lead time).
- One-time fees: onboarding (security review, network setup, private endpoints) ~$12k–$25k depending on VPC complexity; optional SOC2 DPA addendum and audit retainer billed separately.
- KMS/HSM: CMK integration available — pass-through request costs and HSM key storage add ~$500–$1,200/mo depending on vendor.
- Network egress: estimate at $0.02/GB for inter-region egress; if Atlas keeps traffic in a cloud region this is minimal.

Recommendation:
- For Atlas’s stated latency targets and burst profile, I recommend a 2-month Dedicated pilot at the medium reserved commit (2 GPUs equivalent) to validate latency and effective cost (~$1.10 / 1k tokens at 50M). This reduces procurement risk and gives measurable metrics for a full reserved commit.

I attached the updated model and a short-term pilot template. If helpful I can prepare a draft SOW with acceptance criteria (p95/p99 latency targets, availability, error budget) and invoicing terms.
